text:
Andrei Kuzmenko's season has been hard in ways the stat line can't show. He took a leave of absence after his father's death before the season, rejoined the Penguins in early October, and has since spent stretches as a healthy scratch. He returned in Nashville on Saturday after nearly two weeks out and scored his first goal of the year.

That leaves him at one goal and two points in 13 games, about 12.6 minutes a night. The shot volume has been light (13 shots), and the Penguins get only about 44% of the expected goals, our measure of chance quality, at five on five with him on the ice. Pittsburgh has also scored 4.8 fewer goals than its chances deserved while he plays, so some of the empty line is bad luck.

This is still a player who scored 39 goals as a rookie in Vancouver, and our range expects about 25 points if he stays in the lineup. Corey Sznajder's All Three Zones tracking credited him with clean breakouts last season (59% of exits with possession), and Evolving-Hockey had most of his value coming from drawing penalties. The question now: does Saturday's goal earn him the next one.
